title: Memory Manipulation
abstract: arXiv:2610.29847v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We study persuasion that works through memory: a manipulator alters the probabilities with which a Bayesian decision-maker recalls the signals he has received. The decision-maker corrects for the elevated or reduced probabilities of recalling different signals, and this correction disciplines what manipulation can achieve. Manipulation cannot move the average posterior. It backfires on decision-makers with few memories, whose sparse recall is evidence against the favored state, yet it is effective on those with many, who can be led to arbitrarily confident beliefs in the wrong state. It thickens the right tail of the belief distribution and, under Poisson memory, lowers its hazard rate. In a monopoly pricing application, the seller manipulates memory retrieval at high prices, and manipulation in turn raises the optimal price. In a narrative persuasion application, memory manipulation reduces information provision and creates echo chamber

translated_abstract: 本文研究通过记忆起作用的说服机制：操纵者改变贝叶斯决策者回忆其所接收信号的概率。决策者会对不同信号回忆概率的升高或降低进行校正，而这种校正行为限制了操纵所能达到的效果。操纵无法移动平均后验信念。对于记忆较少的决策者，操纵会适得其反，因为其稀疏的回忆本身就构成不利于操纵者所青睐状态的证据；然而对于记忆较多的决策者，操纵却十分有效，能够使其对错误状态形成任意程度的自信信念。操纵会使信念分布的右尾变厚，并且在泊松记忆假设下降低信念分布的风险率。在垄断定价的应用中，卖方在高价格时操纵记忆检索，而这种操纵反过来又提高了最优价格。在叙事说服的应用中，记忆操纵减少了信息提供并制造了回音室效应。
tldr: 本文提出了通过改变贝叶斯决策者对信号回忆概率来实现说服的记忆操纵模型，证明操纵无法改变平均后验信念、且对记忆较少者适得其反，但能使记忆较多者对错误状态形成极度自信的信念，并在垄断定价与叙事说服两个应用中揭示了记忆操纵的经济后果。
en_tdlr: This paper studies persuasion through memory manipulation—altering the probabilities with which a Bayesian decision-maker recalls signals—and shows that while manipulation cannot shift the average posterior and backfires on decision-makers with few memories, it can drive those with many memories to arbitrarily confident wrong beliefs, with applications to monopoly pricing and narrative persuasion.
